title: Aloe vera: a care sheet
text:
Aloe vera is a succulent that stores water in its thick leaves, so it needs water only when the soil has dried completely.
In summer that means watering about every 3 weeks; in winter, once a month is usually enough.
A young plant does not flower: aloe vera usually flowers only after 4 years, sending up a stalk up to 90 cm tall with yellow tube-shaped flowers.
New plants grow as pups around the base of the mother plant, and a pup can be separated once it has 4 or 5 leaves of its own.
The leaves have soft teeth along their edges, and inside each leaf is a clear gel.
Leaves that turn brown or red after a move outdoors are usually getting too much direct sun, not too little water.
Plant it in a clay pot with a drainage hole and a gritty cactus mix, never in plain garden soil.
